title: Policy Weaver: per-customer & per-route tuning playbook with safe apply/rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an automated orchestration layer ('Policy Weaver') that generates per-customer and per-route batching/caching recommendations, converts them to safe config changes, and executes staged applies with automatic verification and rollback. Unlike prior recommenders that produce static suggestions, Policy Weaver will simulate downstream cost/latency effects, synthesize tiered allow/deny lists, and drive canary deployments across Dedicated and Hosted routes with operator gates and audit trails.

Key capabilities to deliver in this ticket scope: 
1) Segmentation profiler: a nightly job that computes customer and route fingerprints (P95 sequence length, average request inter-arrival, model variant mix) and assigns each to a segmentation bucket (e.g., bursty-short, steady-long, conversational).
2) Recommendation engine: rules + ML hybrid that maps segmentation + business tier -> recommended batching window, KV prefetch settings, cache TTL, and whether to enable route-level allowlist/denylist for prefetch. Recommendations are stored as versioned policy drafts.
3) Safe apply pipeline: a dry-run simulator that replays recent traffic from the sandbox (12h) to estimate token-cost delta, latency tail risk (P99), and failure surface. Simulations produce a risk score and suggested rollback triggers.
4) Staged rollout executor: supports dry-run -> canary (1% customers) -> ramp (10/33/100) with automated health checks (latency/5xx/cost deviation/QA eval). Each stage records audit events and an immutable config snapshot.
5) Auto-rollback and human approval: automated abort on health-check violations plus an operator approval webhook for high-risk customers or high-cost delta.
6) Allowlist/denylist manager: per-route rules that can pin customers to safe preset or prevent caching/prefetch for regulated tenants.

Why this matters: current cost tuning is manual and coarse-grained. Policy Weaver reduces operator toil, lowers per-token spend for low-risk segments, and preserves SLOs by enforcing staged verification and fast rollback.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full UI in Console (will add follow-up PM/Design ticket), deep model re-quantization actions, and on-prem installer changes.

Technical approach (high-level):
- Data pipeline: extend ops-telemetry to produce per-customer time-series (seq len, tokens, latency, 5xx, model) into a nightly batch job.
- Simulator: reuse dryrun-sandbox infra (ENG-84021) but add per-route prefetch and KV cache modeling. Simulator will output JSON risk report and synthetic traces.
- Policy store: git-like policy registry (immutable versions, signature) backed by our existing config store.
- Executor: orchestrator service that pulls policy diffs, creates canary rollout plan, and coordinates with runtime to apply dynamic config via RPC.
- Observability: add a dedicated dashboard and alerting on rollout health metrics and cost deviations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Nightly segmentation profiler runs and populates segmentation table for >= 95% active customers (non-empty fingerprints).
- Recommendation engine can produce policy drafts for 100 sample customers; each draft includes batching_window_ms, cache_ttl_sec, prefetch_enabled (bool), allowlist_state (enum).
- Simulator runs on a 12-hour sliding window and produces risk score and P99 latency delta estimate within 10% of observed for two held-out test customers.
- Executor can perform a dry-run and a 1% canary apply on staging with automatic rollback on synthetic latency/5xx injection.
- Audit logs emitted for each policy apply and stored for 90 days.

Metrics to monitor:
- Cost delta per-customer (USD/day) and aggregate weekly savings projection.
- Rollout failure rate and mean time-to-rollback.
- Fraction of customers assigned to each segmentation bucket.

Rollback strategy:
- Fail-fast: any stage health-check violation triggers immediate rollback to previous policy snapshot.
- Time-limited human override: operators can force-commit in emergency after acknowledging risk.
- Postmortem triggers when rollback occurs for >1% of active customers in a calendar day.

Security & compliance notes: customers in regulated tiers will be marked in the segmentation profiler and forced into denylist for prefetch; keys and audit logs obey KMS/HSM retention policy.

Deliverables (this ticket):
- Implementation of segmentation profiler (batch job + test coverage).
- Prototype recommendation engine with rule set and a small ML classifier to validate segmentation mappings.
- Simulator integration + example risk reports for 10 customers.
- Staged rollout executor MVP with dry-run + 1% canary on staging and rollback logic.
- Documentation: internal runbook and PRD link below.
acceptance_criteria: Segmentation profiler populates fingerprints for >=95% of active customers
Recommendation engine emits draft policies for 100 sample customers with required fields
Simulator produces risk reports with <10% error vs held-out test customers
Executor completes dry-run and 1% canary in staging and supports automated rollback
Audit logs written for each apply and retained for 90 days
comments: 2025-01-17 | Marcus Lee: Spike completed for segmentation fingerprints. Initial schema pushed to policy-store. Observed three sensible buckets: bursty-short, steady-long, mixed-interactive.

2025-01-23 | Aisha Patel: Decision - simulator will model KV cache hit probability using simple LRU + TTL model to start; we may swap to learned cache model in a follow-up. Marked security constraints: regulated customers must be denylisted for prefetch.
2025-01-29 | Kenji Tanaka: Implemented canary coordinator with staged percentages. Staging dry-run showed ~18% cost drop for bursty-short group with negligible P99 increase in synthetic runs.

2025-02-04 | Marcus Lee: Integration test failing intermittently on rollback path (race between executor and runtime version pin). Investigating locking semantics; added temporary guard that aborts if version mismatch detected.
2025-02-06 | Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to require audit logs retained 90 days. Added runbook link and flagged follow-up UX ticket for Console exposure.
